4. Problem Files 
4.4. Problem Data Blocks 
4.4.N. *Survey Data Block 
4.4.11. *Survey Data Block 
The purpose of a survey is to change the value of one or more input parameters and 
determine the effect on the trajectories. This is called a tradeoff study or sensitivity 
study. Trajectories are computed for all values of the survey variable. 
As noted in Section 4.1, any numerical value in the problem file can be systematically 
varied by defining a survey. For example, 
*initial 
alt=surv-1 lat=O long=O wk1200 
has the variable alt set to the value of survey one. The keyword sum-1 is aplacehold- 
er for the actual value that will be used when the problem is run. The actual value is 
determined from the corresponding *survey data block. The survey numbers are 
used to relate the survey keywords to the survey data blocks, so s u n 4  corresponds 
to the *survey 1 data block, sum-2 corresponds to the *survey 2 data block, and so 
on. 
The sum-1, surv-2, etc., keywords control which variables in the problem file are 
modified by the survey. The *survey data blocks control the values assigned to these 
variables. In the above example, the variable aZt in the *initial data block is set to 
sum-l, so there must be a corresponding *survey 1 data block in the problem that 
assigns values for the initial altitude. 
For example, 
*survey 
1 alto 10=40000 hi=80000 inc=20000 
says to run three cases with the initial altitude set to 40,000,60,000, 
and 80,000 ft. 
TAOS substitutes the survey value everywhere the surv-n keyword is found in the 
problem file. So more than one variable in the problem file can be set to the survey 
value. 
Survey Numbers and Names 
The survey data block begins with the *survey data block name and the survey num- 
ber. Survey numbers are normally assigned in sequence beginning with one. Any 
number of survey loops can be defined. The surveys form nested loops with the low- 
est-numbered survey the inner most and the highest-numbered survey the outer 
most, 
A survey variable name follows the survey number. This name must be unique from 
other output variable names. It is used in the EGS database files for plotting the re- 
sults of a s~rvey.~ 
In the example above, the EGS database would contain one or more 
trajectories associated with aZt0=40000, another set of trajectories associated with 
aZt0=60000, and so on.

one method where the values take on incremental values. A starting value is given,
